This page maps the workshop into time. Three formats are supported — pick the one that matches your situation, or build your own from the session table at the bottom.

## Reading materials and tools

### Required, before you start

- [Setup](Setup.qmd) — one-button install that gets you from a fresh laptop to "ready to run Tutorial 01" (\~30–60 minutes, run **before** Day 1)
- [Software](Software.qmd) — the package list that Setup installs
- [Datasets](Datasets.qmd) — how datasets are accessed (most are auto-installed, no manual download needed)

### Recommended companion books (any one of these)

- [Single-cell best practices (Heumos *et al.*)](https://www.sc-best-practices.org/) — the canonical online textbook for the field
- [Orchestrating Single-Cell Analysis with Bioconductor (OSCA)](https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA/) — the Bioconductor / `SingleCellExperiment` perspective
- [Analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data (Sanger / EBI course)](https://www.singlecellcourse.org/) — self-paced, free

### Tools

- A laptop with R ≥ 4.4, RStudio, and \~10 GB free disk
- A terminal with `ssh` (only for the Talapas advanced track)
- A GitHub account (for cloning this repository and following the version-control workflow in Appendix E)

## Format A — Two-week intensive (11 sessions, in-person summer workshop)

Designed for an immersive 2-week format. Each session is **\~3 hours** total: 45–60 min of lecture + 90–120 min of tutorial work + Q&A. Day 11 is a project work-day where students apply the workflow to a dataset of their choice.

| Day | Session | Lecture | Tutorial(s) | Reading (sc-best-practices.org) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Welcome + scRNA-seq fundamentals** | [Lec 00 — Bulk vs scRNA-seq](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_00_Bulk_vs_scRNAseq.html) | (lecture only — sets up the rest) | Ch. 1: Introduction |
| 2 | **Quality control & doublets** | [Lec 01 — Pre-processing](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_01_Preprocessing.html) | [Tut 01 — QC](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_01_QC_Preprocessing.html) | Ch. 6: Quality control |
| 3 | **Dim reduction & clustering** | [Lec 02 — DimRed/Integration](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_02_DimRed_Integration_Clustering.html) | [Tut 02 — DimRed/Clustering](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_02_DimReduction_Clustering.html) | Ch. 7–8: Dim reduction & clustering |
| 4 | **Marker genes & manual annotation** | [Lec 03 — Markers/Annotation](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_03_Markers_Annotation.html) | [Tut 03 — Markers/Annotation](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_03_Markers_Annotation.html) | Ch. 9: Annotation |
| 5 | **Multi-sample integration** | [Lec 02 (integration sections)](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_02_DimRed_Integration_Clustering.html#step-6-integration-batch-correction) | [Tut 04 — Integration](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_04_Integration.html) | Ch. 11: Integration |
| 6 | **Differential expression — DESeq2 + pseudobulk** | [Lec 04 — Pseudobulk DE](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_04_Pseudobulk_DE.html) | [Tut 05 — DESeq2 Primer](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_05_Primer_DESeq2_Basics.html) + [Tut 06 — Pseudobulk DE](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_06_Pseudobulk_DE.html) | Ch. 12: DE |
| 7 | **Functional analysis** | [Lec 05 — Functional Analysis](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_05_FunctionalAnalysis.html) | [Tut 07 — Functional Analysis](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_07_FunctionalAnalysis.html) | Ch. 13: Gene-set analysis |
| 8 | **Differential abundance** | [Lec 06 — Differential Abundance](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_06_DifferentialAbundance.html) | [Tut 08 — Differential Abundance](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_08_DifferentialAbundance.html) | Ch. 14: Compositional analysis |
| 9 | **Reference-based annotation + ATAC** | [Lec 07 — Reference Annotation](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_07_Reference_Annotation.html) + [Lec 08 — ATAC-seq](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_08_ATACseq.html) | [Tut 09 — Reference Annotation](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_09_Reference_Annotation.html) + [Tut 10 — scATAC-seq](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_10_scATACseq_Signac.html) | Ch. 9, 24 |
| 10 | **WGCNA + Spatial + FAIR** | [Lec 09 — WGCNA](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_09_WGCNA.html) + [Lec 10 — Spatial](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_10_Spatial.html) + [Lec 11 — FAIR](Lecture_Folder/Lecture_11_FAIR_DataSharing.html) | [Tut 11 — WGCNA](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_11_WGCNA.html) + [Tut 12 — Spatial](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_12_Spatial_Transcriptomics.html) + [Tut 13 — FAIR](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_13_FAIR_Metadata.html) | Ch. 23, 27 |
| 11 | **Capstone work-day** | [Capstone Mini-Project guide](Capstone.html) | (work on your own dataset; instructor available for help) | — |

## Format B — Term-long course (10–12 weeks, graduate seminar)

Designed for a one-quarter or one-semester graduate course, **one session per week**, each \~2 hours of lecture + students do the tutorial on their own time before the next session.

| Week | Topic | Lecture | Tutorial assignment due before next week |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | scRNA-seq fundamentals | Lec 00 | (read the lecture; complete Setup) |
| 2 | QC & doublets | Lec 01 | Tut 01 |
| 3 | Dim reduction & clustering | Lec 02 (PCA + clustering halves) | Tut 02 |
| 4 | Marker-based annotation | Lec 03 | Tut 03 |
| 5 | Multi-sample integration | Lec 02 (integration half) | Tut 04 |
| 6 | DE — DESeq2 fundamentals | Lec 04 (Part 1) | Tut 05 |
| 7 | DE — pseudobulk on scRNA-seq | Lec 04 (Parts 2–3) | Tut 06 |
| 8 | Functional analysis | Lec 05 | Tut 07 |
| 9 | Differential abundance | Lec 06 | Tut 08 |
| 10 | Reference-based annotation | Lec 07 | Tut 09 |
| 11 | scATAC-seq + WGCNA + FAIR | Lec 08 + 09 + 11 | Tut 10 + 11 + 13 (pick two of three) |
| 12 | Capstone presentations | (student talks) | Capstone report due |

Spatial Transcriptomics (Lec 10 + Tut 12) and the Talapas Advanced track (Cell Ranger raw-data tutorials) sit outside this 12-week block as **bonus** material — students can pick one as a self-study project.

## Format C — Self-paced

If you're working through this on your own, the recommended order is just the lecture/tutorial numbering. Plan for:

- \~25–35 hours total for Lectures 00–07 + Tutorials 01–09 (the core scRNA-seq workflow)
- +\~10 hours for the bonus modules (ATAC, WGCNA, Spatial, FAIR)
- +\~10 hours for the Talapas advanced track (Cell Ranger raw-data + SLURM)

A reasonable pace is **one lecture/tutorial pair per week** (1–3 hours per week), giving \~3 months for the full set. Faster if you're already comfortable with R and have done bulk RNA-seq before.

## Workshop preparation checklist

A week before Day 1 (or your first self-study session):

::: callout-note
**Pre-workshop checklist**

- [ ] Install R ≥ 4.4 and current RStudio Desktop ([Software](Software.qmd) page lists exact versions)
- [ ] Run the [Setup](Setup.qmd) install script (\~30–60 min — *do this before Day 1, not the morning of*)
- [ ] Verify install: open R, paste the verification block from Setup, confirm all packages load
- [ ] Clone or download this repository
- [ ] Bookmark the workshop website
- [ ] If using Talapas: request an account at <https://racs.uoregon.edu/request-access> and join the workshop's PIRG (this can take a week)
- [ ] (Optional) Skim Lecture 00 the night before Day 1 — \~20 min, primes the rest

If anything errors during Setup, see the [FAQ](FAQ.qmd) — most common issues are documented. If your install errors aren't in the FAQ, post on the workshop chat channel.
:::
